name: Atlassian Statuspage
summary: Statuspage hosts public, private and audience-specific status pages. The free public plan covers 100 subscribers and 25 components. Paid public plans run from $29 to $1,499 a month and raise the subscriber, team member and notification limits.

facts.text: Incident updates move through the states from investigating to resolved, and subscribers can be notified by email, text message and other channels the page lists.
The Uptime Showcase feature displays historical uptime to current and prospective customers.
SMS and webhook notifications start on the Startup plan. Slack and Microsoft Teams notifications are available on every public plan, including Free.
Component subscriptions and role-based access control start on the Business plan.
Private pages are priced separately by employee count, from $79 a month for 50 employees. Audience-specific pages start at $300 a month.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 100 subscribers, 25 components, 2 team members, 2 metrics. Email, Slack and Microsoft Teams notifications

plans.name: Hobby
plans.notes: 250 subscribers, 5 team members, 5 metrics, custom domain. No SMS or webhook notifications

plans.name: Startup
plans.notes: 1,000 subscribers, 10 team members, 10 metrics. SMS and webhook notifications. Team member SSO with Atlassian Guard

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: 5,000 subscribers, 25 team members, 25 metrics. Component subscriptions and role-based access control

hiddenCosts: Prices are listed per month. The FAQ says yearly billing is set up manually and needs a signed order form.
The page shows a dollar sign without naming the currency.
Private pages start at $79 a month, and audience-specific pages start at $300 a month. Both are priced separately from the public plans.
